newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast prods stready to lower after Gulf storm.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast prods stready to lower after Gulf storm.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined products were steady to lower Friday, reflecting the light volume of trade ahead of the weekend, brokers said.
Downward pressure came from products futures, especially August unleaded gasoline on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), which fell 1.84 cents a gallon to 60.05 cents.
The drop came after a tropical storm in the U.S. Gulf of Mexico left the key production and refiner region unscathed. NYMEX energy prices generally influence the West Coast spot markets.
Traders offered July and August CARB gasoline to Los Angeles refineries at 59 cents and 60 cents a gallon, traders said, 1.00 cent under Thursday.
CARB diesel was talked between 55.50 and 56.50 cents a gallon, a half cent under yesterday.
State-mandated CARB gasoline fell in line with L.A., and was talked between 60 and 61 cents a gallon. CARB diesel fuel remained about five cents under L.A. due to overproductionn.
